rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable critical lower limb ischaemia with foot symptoms / Diagnose probable peripheral vascular disease from foot symptoms
rule_level_problems.problem: The page uses almost the same phrase twice ('Muscle pain in legs or buttocks on exercise' in the red box; 'muscle pain in legs or buttocks' in the PVD flowchart branch) and the file codes them differently: 'Intermittent claudication' for the CLI rule, 'Muscle pain' + finding_site (Lower limb structure / Buttock structure) for the PVD rule. The two check lists therefore contain three different muscle-pain items and the two rules do not see each other's recordings: a nurse who records lower-limb muscle pain (the PVD check item) together with foot pain at rest will not trigger critical limb ischaemia (the urgent diagnosis), and a recorded claudication with generalised foot pain may not trigger PVD (it depends on whether a finding without a finding_site satisfies a site-constrained evidence clause). Suggest the CLI rule accept either form (or the PVD branch add Intermittent claudication), so that the urgent path is not lost on a wording choice.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded (fracture, acute and critical limb ischaemia as probable diagnoses feeding an Urgent priority evaluation), and all five 'X likely' conclusions on the page have probable rules with the flowchart's logic and exact or nearest SNOMED concepts. The most consequential problem is inconsistent coding of 'muscle pain in legs or buttocks': the red box uses Intermittent claudication while the PVD branch uses site-qualified Muscle pain, so the urgent critical-limb-ischaemia rule can be missed when the nurse records the PVD form. The diabetes/PVD 'foot at risk' criteria block is not encoded at all (borderline scope), and the neuropathy criterion drops 'constant' and 'worse at night'.
